notes: Also 'home' in general ('uwi sa bahay'), even when you live in a condo.

examples.tl: Nasa bahay lang ako buong araw.
examples.en: I was just at home all day.
examples.taglish: Nasa bahay lang ako buong araw, WFH.

examples.tl: Uwi na tayo sa bahay, traffic na mamaya.
examples.en: Let's go home, it'll be traffic later.

notes: Said as in English. 'Unit' = your apartment; 'tower'/'building' for the block. 'Apartment' usually means a cheaper walk-up.

examples.tl: Punta ka sa condo ko mamaya, mag-order tayo.
examples.en: Come to my condo later, let's order food.

examples.tl: Ilang floor ang unit mo?
examples.en: What floor is your unit on?

notes: Formal spelling 'kuwarto'. Bedroom = kwarto; 'silid' is literary.

examples.tl: Nasa kwarto ko ang charger, kunin mo lang.
examples.en: The charger is in my room, just get it.

examples.tl: Isang kwarto lang ang unit namin, studio type.
examples.en: Our unit has just one room, studio type.

examples.tl: Nasa kusina si Ate, nagluluto ng ulam.
examples.en: Ate is in the kitchen cooking the main dish.

examples.tl: Maliit ang kusina sa condo, induction lang ang gamit namin.
examples.en: The condo kitchen is small, we only use an induction stove.

notes: The bathroom at home. In public places people say 'CR'.

examples.tl: Nasa banyo pa siya, naliligo.
examples.en: She's still in the bathroom, showering.

examples.tl: Barado ang drain sa banyo, tumawag ka sa admin.
examples.en: The bathroom drain is clogged, call the admin.

notes: From 'comfort room'. The everyday word for any toilet outside the home; 'banyo' is the one at home.

examples.tl: Saan ang CR dito?
examples.en: Where's the restroom here?

examples.tl: Pupunta lang ako ng CR, bantayan mo ang bag ko.
examples.en: I'm just going to the restroom, watch my bag.

taglish: Mag-CR lang ako, wait ka diyan.
notes: Nag-CR, nagsi-CR. Very common and polite enough for any setting.

examples.tl: Mag-CR lang ako, sandali.
examples.en: I'll just use the restroom, one sec.

examples.tl: Pwede ba akong mag-CR sa inyo?
examples.en: Can I use your bathroom?

examples.tl: Nasa sala ang TV at ang mga bisita.
examples.en: The TV and the guests are in the living room.

examples.tl: Matulog ka na lang sa sala, may sofa bed.
examples.en: Just sleep in the living room, there's a sofa bed.

notes: 'Pintuan' = doorway, also used for the door itself.

examples.tl: Isara mo ang pinto, lalabas ang lamig ng aircon.
examples.en: Close the door, the aircon cold will get out.

examples.tl: May kumakatok sa pinto, baka delivery.
examples.en: Someone's knocking at the door, maybe a delivery.

examples.tl: Buksan mo ang bintana, amoy luto sa loob.
examples.en: Open the window, it smells of cooking inside.

examples.tl: Hindi nabubuksan ang bintana sa condo namin.
examples.en: The windows in our condo can't be opened.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang susi sa loob, tawagin natin ang guard.
examples.en: I left the key inside, let's call the guard.
examples.taglish: Naiwan ko ang susi sa loob, na-lock out ako!

examples.tl: Nasaan ang susi ng unit? Hindi ko mahanap.
examples.en: Where's the unit key? I can't find it.

examples.tl: Hindi ko pa naaayos ang kama ko.
examples.en: I haven't made my bed yet.

examples.tl: Queen size ang kama namin, kasya pa sa kwarto.
examples.en: Our bed is queen size, it still fits in the room.

notes: Root upo (sit). 'Silya' also used for a chair.

examples.tl: Kulang ang upuan, may bisita tayo mamaya.
examples.en: We don't have enough chairs, we have guests later.

examples.tl: May upuan ba sa labas ng clinic?
examples.en: Are there seats outside the clinic?

examples.tl: Ilagay mo lang sa mesa ang grocery.
examples.en: Just put the groceries on the table.

examples.tl: Walang mesa sa unit, sa sofa kami kumakain.
examples.en: There's no table in the unit, we eat on the sofa.

notes: Lights are 'buksan' (open) and 'patayin' (kill), not 'isara'. 'Bukas ang ilaw' = the light is on.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang ilaw bago ka matulog.
examples.en: Turn off the light before you sleep.

examples.tl: Buksan mo ang ilaw, madilim na.
examples.en: Turn on the light, it's dark already.

notes: Always 'aircon', never 'AC'. Hinaan = turn down, lakasan = turn up.

examples.tl: Ang init! Buksan natin ang aircon.
examples.en: It's so hot! Let's turn on the aircon.

examples.tl: Mahal ang kuryente kapag maghapon ang aircon.
examples.en: Electricity is expensive if the aircon runs all day.

notes: Many people just say 'electric fan' or 'fan'.

examples.tl: Bentilador lang muna, mahal ang kuryente.
examples.en: Just the fan for now, electricity is expensive.

examples.tl: Itutok mo sa akin ang bentilador, pawis na ako.
examples.en: Point the fan at me, I'm sweating.

notes: Drinking water is delivered in 5-gallon 'galon' refills.

examples.tl: Walang tubig sa buong building ngayon.
examples.en: There's no water in the whole building right now.

examples.tl: Pabili ng tubig, isang galon.
examples.en: Please buy water, one gallon.

notes: 'Nawalan ng kuryente' = power went out. Meralco is the Manila provider.

examples.tl: Nawalan ng kuryente kagabi, grabe ang init.
examples.en: The power went out last night, the heat was terrible.

examples.tl: Mahal ang kuryente ngayong buwan, 4,000 ang bill ko.
examples.en: Electricity is expensive this month, my bill is 4,000.

notes: Filipinos say 'brownout' for any outage; 'blackout' is rare.

examples.tl: May brownout sa Makati kanina, dalawang oras.
examples.en: There was a power outage in Makati earlier, two hours.

examples.tl: Brownout ulit? Walang wifi tuloy.
examples.en: Power outage again? So no wifi.

notes: 'Magtapon ng basura' = take out the trash. Condos have a garbage room per floor.

examples.tl: Ilabas mo na ang basura, mabaho na.
examples.en: Take out the trash now, it stinks already.

examples.tl: Saan ang tapunan ng basura dito sa floor?
examples.en: Where's the trash chute on this floor?

notes: Labahan = clothes to be washed, or the washing area. 'Labada' = a batch of laundry. 'Laundry' also common.

examples.tl: Dami ng labahan, dalhin na natin sa laundry shop.
examples.en: So much laundry, let's take it to the laundry shop.

examples.tl: Nasa labahan pa ang jeans mo.
examples.en: Your jeans are still in the laundry.

notes: Root laba. Naglaba, naglalaba, maglalaba. 'Labahin' = wash (it).

examples.tl: Maglalaba ako bukas, Sabado.
examples.en: I'll do laundry tomorrow, Saturday.

examples.tl: Naglaba si Ate kanina, nasa sampayan ang mga damit.
examples.en: Ate did the laundry earlier, the clothes are on the line.

examples.tl: Pakiplantsa ang polo ko para bukas.
examples.en: Please iron my polo shirt for tomorrow.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang plantsa? Gusot ang damit ko.
examples.en: Where's the iron? My clothes are wrinkled.

notes: 'Ipaplantsa' = have it ironed (at the laundry shop).

examples.tl: Hindi ako marunong magplantsa, dinadala ko sa laundry.
examples.en: I don't know how to iron, I take it to the laundry.

examples.tl: Nagplantsa si Ate ng mga polo ko kanina.
examples.en: Ate ironed my polos earlier.

notes: Walis tambo = soft indoor broom; walis tingting = stiff outdoor broom.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang walis? Natapon ang bigas.
examples.en: Where's the broom? The rice spilled.

examples.tl: Walis tambo sa sala, walis tingting sa labas.
examples.en: Soft broom for the living room, stiff broom for outside.

notes: 'Walisin' = sweep (it/the floor).

examples.tl: Magwalis ka muna bago mag-mop.
examples.en: Sweep first before you mop.

examples.tl: Nagwalis na ako ng sala, ikaw na sa kusina.
examples.en: I already swept the living room, you do the kitchen.

notes: The surface you walk on. A building level is 'floor' or 'palapag'.

examples.tl: Basa ang sahig, mag-ingat ka.
examples.en: The floor is wet, be careful.

examples.tl: Mag-mop tayo ng sahig, madumi na.
examples.en: Let's mop the floor, it's dirty already.

examples.tl: Pwede bang magbutas sa dingding? Tanong muna sa admin.
examples.en: Can we drill into the wall? Ask the admin first.

examples.tl: Manipis ang dingding, rinig ang kapitbahay.
examples.en: The wall is thin, you can hear the neighbor.

examples.tl: Sira ang elevator, hagdan muna tayo.
examples.en: The elevator is broken, let's take the stairs.

examples.tl: Nasa 3rd floor lang ako, hagdan na lang.
examples.en: I'm just on the 3rd floor, I'll take the stairs.

notes: 'Lift' is not used. Also just 'elev'.

examples.tl: Ang tagal ng elevator sa building namin tuwing umaga.
examples.en: The elevator in our building takes forever in the morning.

examples.tl: Isa lang ang gumaganang elevator ngayon.
examples.en: Only one elevator is working right now.

examples.tl: Nasa lobby na ang Grab mo.
examples.en: Your Grab is already in the lobby.

examples.tl: Pakikuha ang package ko sa lobby.
examples.en: Please pick up my package at the lobby.

notes: Address as 'Kuya guard' or 'Sir'. 'Gwardya' is understood, 'sekyu' is slang.

examples.tl: Iwan mo lang sa guard ang package ko.
examples.en: Just leave my package with the guard.

examples.tl: Tanungin mo ang guard kung saan ang visitor parking.
examples.en: Ask the guard where the visitor parking is.

notes: The polite term. 'Katulong' still common; 'yaya' = nanny. Address her as 'Ate' or 'Manang'.

examples.tl: Tuwing Sabado lang pumupunta ang kasambahay namin.
examples.en: Our helper only comes on Saturdays.

examples.tl: Masipag ang kasambahay nila, pati plantsa gawa niya.
examples.en: Their helper is hardworking, she even does the ironing.

examples.tl: Maingay ang kapitbahay namin tuwing gabi, may karaoke.
examples.en: Our neighbors are noisy every night, they have karaoke.

examples.tl: Mabait ang kapitbahay ko, binigyan ako ng ulam.
examples.en: My neighbor is kind, she gave me some food.

notes: 'Nagre-rent' or 'nangungupahan' = renting. Most people just say 'rent'.

examples.tl: Kailan ang due ng upa mo?
examples.en: When is your rent due?

examples.tl: Tumaas ang upa namin ng 2,000 ngayong taon.
examples.en: Our rent went up by 2,000 this year.

notes: Monthly condo fees, often just 'dues'. Separate from rent and Meralco.

examples.tl: Nagtaas ulit ang association dues sa condo.
examples.en: The condo association dues went up again.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba sa upa ang dues?
examples.en: Are the dues included in the rent?

notes: The condo management office. Also 'admin office'.

examples.tl: Mag-report ka sa admin, tumutulo ang tubo sa banyo.
examples.en: Report it to the admin, the bathroom pipe is leaking.

examples.tl: Sarado ang admin office tuwing Linggo.
examples.en: The admin office is closed on Sundays.

notes: 'Nakakandado' = locked. For door locks people also say 'naka-lock'.

examples.tl: Nakakandado ang gate pagkatapos ng alas-diyes.
examples.en: The gate is padlocked after ten o'clock.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng kandado para sa bike mo.
examples.en: Buy a padlock for your bike.

examples.tl: Nasa gate na ang delivery mo.
examples.en: Your delivery is at the gate.

examples.tl: Kailangan ng ID sa gate ng village.
examples.en: You need an ID at the village gate.

examples.tl: Barado ang lababo, tawagan natin ang maintenance.
examples.en: The sink is clogged, let's call maintenance.

examples.tl: Tambak na ang hugasan sa lababo.
examples.en: The dishes are piled up in the sink.

notes: Filipinos say 'ref', not 'fridge'. 'Tira' = leftovers.

examples.tl: May tira pa sa ref, i-microwave mo lang.
examples.en: There are leftovers in the fridge, just microwave them.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa ref ang gatas, masisira.
examples.en: Put the milk in the fridge, it'll spoil.

notes: Many condos ban gas, so 'induction' is common.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang kalan, kumukulo na.
examples.en: Turn off the stove, it's boiling already.

examples.tl: Walang gas na kalan dito, induction ang gamit.
examples.en: No gas stove here, we use induction.

examples.tl: Hugasan mo na ang kaldero, may natirang kanin.
examples.en: Wash the pot now, there's leftover rice in it.

examples.tl: Malaking kaldero ang gamitin mo sa sinigang.
examples.en: Use the big pot for the sinigang.

examples.tl: Painitin mo muna ang kawali bago ilagay ang itlog.
examples.en: Heat the pan first before putting in the egg.

examples.tl: Non-stick ang kawali, huwag kang gumamit ng metal.
examples.en: The pan is non-stick, don't use metal.

examples.tl: Kuha ka ng plato, kain na tayo.
examples.en: Get a plate, let's eat.

examples.tl: Dalawang plato lang ang malinis, hugasan mo na ang iba.
examples.en: Only two plates are clean, wash the rest.

examples.tl: Nabasag ang baso, ingat sa bubog.
examples.en: The glass broke, careful of the shards.

examples.tl: Kuha ka ng baso, may Coke sa ref.
examples.en: Get a glass, there's Coke in the fridge.

notes: Filipinos eat with spoon and fork; the spoon does the cutting.

examples.tl: Kutsara at tinidor lang, walang kutsilyo.
examples.en: Just spoon and fork, no knife.

examples.tl: Pahingi ng kutsara, pang-sabaw.
examples.en: Can I have a spoon, for the soup.

examples.tl: Wala akong tinidor, kutsara lang ang binigay.
examples.en: I don't have a fork, they only gave a spoon.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa mesa ang tinidor at kutsara.
examples.en: Put the forks and spoons on the table.

notes: Every household has one. Said in English.

examples.tl: Isaksak mo ang rice cooker, magsaing na tayo.
examples.en: Plug in the rice cooker, let's cook rice.

examples.tl: Naka-warm pa ang rice cooker, may kanin pa.
examples.en: The rice cooker is still on warm, there's rice left.

notes: Root saing. Bigas = uncooked rice, kanin = cooked rice.

examples.tl: Magsaing ka na, uuwi si Mama ng alas-sais.
examples.en: Cook rice now, Mom is coming home at six.

examples.tl: Nagsaing ako ng dalawang tasa, sapat na sa atin.
examples.en: I cooked two cups of rice, that's enough for us.

examples.tl: Isara mo ang kurtina, sobrang init sa hapon.
examples.en: Close the curtain, it's so hot in the afternoon.

examples.tl: Blackout curtain ang binili ko para makatulog.
examples.en: I bought blackout curtains so I can sleep.

examples.tl: Dalawa ang unan ko, hindi ako makatulog sa isa.
examples.en: I use two pillows, I can't sleep with one.

examples.tl: Palitan mo ang punda ng unan, Linggo na.
examples.en: Change the pillowcase, it's Sunday already.

examples.tl: Kumot pa, malamig ang aircon.
examples.en: More blanket please, the aircon is cold.

examples.tl: Nasa labahan ang kumot, gamitin mo muna ang isa.
examples.en: The blanket is in the wash, use the other one for now.

notes: Most people just say 'towel'.

examples.tl: Nasa banyo ang malinis na tuwalya.
examples.en: The clean towel is in the bathroom.

examples.tl: Pahiram ng towel, nakalimutan ko sa condo.
examples.en: Lend me a towel, I forgot mine at the condo.

notes: Sabong panlaba = laundry detergent; sabong panghugas = dish soap.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang sabon sa banyo.
examples.en: The soap in the bathroom is used up.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng sabong panlaba, yung powder.
examples.en: Buy laundry detergent, the powder kind.

notes: Sold in tiny sachets at sari-sari stores.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang shampoo, isama mo sa grocery list.
examples.en: The shampoo is finished, add it to the grocery list.

examples.tl: Sachet lang ng shampoo ang binili ko, pang-isang linggo.
examples.en: I only bought shampoo sachets, enough for a week.

notes: 'Colgate' is used as the generic word by many.

examples.tl: Pabili ng toothpaste, kahit anong brand.
examples.en: Please buy toothpaste, any brand.

examples.tl: Wala nang Colgate, konti na lang.
examples.en: There's almost no toothpaste left.

notes: Many public CRs have no tissue; bring your own.

examples.tl: Walang tissue sa CR, magdala ka ng sarili mo.
examples.en: There's no tissue in the restroom, bring your own.

examples.tl: Pahingi ng tissue, natapon ang kape.
examples.en: Can I have a tissue, the coffee spilled.

examples.tl: Mag-ipon tayo ng tubig sa timba, may water interruption bukas.
examples.en: Let's store water in the bucket, there's a water cut tomorrow.

examples.tl: Timba at tabo lang, walang shower sa boarding house.
examples.en: Just a bucket and dipper, no shower at the boarding house.

notes: The plastic dipper beside every Filipino toilet; used for washing and bucket baths.

examples.tl: Walang bidet dito, tabo lang ang gamit.
examples.en: No bidet here, we just use the dipper.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang tabo? Sira ang shower.
examples.en: Where's the dipper? The shower is broken.

notes: 'Isampay' = hang up to dry. Many condos ban drying on the balcony.

examples.tl: Isampay mo sa sampayan, bawal sa balcony sabi ng admin.
examples.en: Hang it on the drying rack, the admin says the balcony is off limits.

examples.tl: Puno na ang sampayan, dami ng nilabhan.
examples.en: The clothesline is full, so much got washed.

examples.tl: May washing machine na kami, hindi na kailangan ng laundry shop.
examples.en: We have a washing machine now, no need for the laundry shop.

examples.tl: Sira ang washing machine, umiikot pero hindi nag-spin.
examples.en: The washing machine is broken, it turns but won't spin.

notes: Drop-off wash-dry-fold, charged per kilo. Every condo area has several.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo sa laundry shop, per kilo ang bayad.
examples.en: Take it to the laundry shop, they charge per kilo.

examples.tl: Kukunin ko ang labada sa laundry shop mamaya.
examples.en: I'll pick up the laundry from the shop later.

notes: Root gising. Gumising, gumigising, gigising. 'Gisingin mo ako' = wake me up.

examples.tl: Gumising ako ng alas-sais para hindi ma-late.
examples.en: I woke up at six so I wouldn't be late.

examples.tl: Gisingin mo ako ng alas-singko, may flight ako.
examples.en: Wake me up at five, I have a flight.

notes: Different from gumising (wake up). 'Ayaw kong bumangon' = I don't want to get up.

examples.tl: Gising na ako pero ayaw ko pang bumangon.
examples.en: I'm awake but I don't want to get up yet.

examples.tl: Bumangon ka na, alas-otso na!
examples.en: Get up, it's eight already!

notes: Root ligo. Naligo, naliligo, maliligo. Covers showers too; 'mag-shower' also heard.

examples.tl: Maligo ka muna bago tayo umalis.
examples.en: Shower first before we leave.

examples.tl: Naligo na ako, bihis na lang.
examples.en: I've showered, I just need to get dressed.

notes: The everyday form. 'Magsipilyo' is the native word, less used in Manila.

examples.tl: Nag-toothbrush na ako, tulog na ako.
examples.en: I've brushed my teeth, I'm going to sleep.

examples.tl: Mag-toothbrush ka muna bago lumabas, amoy bawang.
examples.en: Brush your teeth before going out, you smell of garlic.

notes: Root bihis. Also 'change clothes'. 'Bihis na' = already dressed.

examples.tl: Magbihis ka na, nasa lobby na ang Grab.
examples.en: Get dressed, the Grab is already in the lobby.

examples.tl: Magbibihis lang ako, basa ako sa ulan.
examples.en: I'll just change, I got wet in the rain.

notes: 'Mag-almusal' = to eat breakfast. 'Agahan' is also used.

examples.tl: Ano ang almusal natin? Tapsilog?
examples.en: What's our breakfast? Tapsilog?

examples.tl: Hindi ako nag-almusal, kape lang.
examples.en: I didn't have breakfast, just coffee.

notes: 'Mananghalian' = to eat lunch. 'Lunch' itself is very common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Saan tayo mananghalian? Sa food court?
examples.en: Where shall we have lunch? The food court?

examples.tl: Baon ko ang tanghalian ko, tira kagabi.
examples.en: I packed my lunch, last night's leftovers.

notes: 'Maghapunan' = to eat dinner. 'Dinner' is also common.

examples.tl: Ano ang hapunan? Mag-order na lang tayo.
examples.en: What's for dinner? Let's just order.

examples.tl: Maghapunan ka muna bago umuwi.
examples.en: Have dinner first before going home.

notes: Root tulog. Natulog, natutulog, matutulog. 'Tulog na' = asleep already.

examples.tl: Matulog ka na, maaga ka bukas.
examples.en: Go to sleep, you're up early tomorrow.

examples.tl: Alas-dos na ako natulog kagabi, antok ako ngayon.
examples.en: I slept at two last night, I'm sleepy now.

notes: Root alis. Umalis, umaalis, aalis. 'Alis na tayo' = let's go.

examples.tl: Umalis ako ng condo ng alas-siyete, late pa rin.
examples.en: I left the condo at seven, still late.

examples.tl: Aalis na ako, lock mo ang pinto.
examples.en: I'm leaving now, lock the door.

notes: Root uwi. Umuwi, umuuwi, uuwi. 'Uwi na' = heading home. 'Pauwi' = on the way home.

examples.tl: Uuwi na ako, traffic na mamaya.
examples.en: I'm going home now, it'll be traffic later.

examples.tl: Anong oras ka umuwi kagabi?
examples.en: What time did you get home last night?

notes: Root luto. Nagluto, nagluluto, magluluto. 'Lutuin' = cook (it). 'Luto na' = cooked/ready.

examples.tl: Magluluto ako ng adobo mamaya, kain ka dito.
examples.en: I'll cook adobo later, eat here.

examples.tl: Hindi ako nagluluto, puro Grab food lang.
examples.en: I don't cook, just Grab food all the time.

notes: Root linis. Naglinis, naglilinis, maglilinis. 'Linisin' = clean (it).

examples.tl: Maglilinis ako ng unit bukas, Linggo.
examples.en: I'll clean the unit tomorrow, Sunday.

examples.tl: Linisin mo ang banyo, may amag na.
examples.en: Clean the bathroom, there's mold already.

notes: Root hugas. For dishes and hands. Clothes = maglaba; body = maligo.

examples.tl: Maghugas ka ng kamay bago kumain.
examples.en: Wash your hands before eating.

examples.tl: Ako na ang maghuhugas ng plato, ikaw na sa basura.
examples.en: I'll wash the dishes, you take out the trash.

notes: Root pahinga. Also 'mag-rest'. 'Pahinga muna' = rest first.

examples.tl: Magpahinga ka muna, mukhang pagod ka.
examples.en: Rest for a while, you look tired.

examples.tl: Day off ko bukas, magpapahinga lang ako sa condo.
examples.en: It's my day off tomorrow, I'll just rest at the condo.

notes: Root ayos. 'Ayusin mo' = fix/arrange it. Also 'mag-ayos' = get ready (hair, face).

examples.tl: Mag-ayos ka ng kwarto mo, nagkalat.
examples.en: Tidy up your room, it's a mess.

examples.tl: Mag-aayos lang ako, five minutes.
examples.en: I'll just get ready, five minutes.

notes: Root ligpit. Putting things back in place; 'ligpitin mo' = put it away. Also for clearing the table.

examples.tl: Magligpit ka ng mga damit mo sa sala.
examples.en: Put away your clothes in the living room.

examples.tl: Ligpitin na natin ang mesa, tapos na kumain.
examples.en: Let's clear the table, we're done eating.

notes: 'Magkalat' = make a mess; 'nagkalat' = messy / scattered. 'Makalat' = messy (adj).

examples.tl: Dami ng kalat, dumating ang mga pamangkin ko.
examples.en: What a mess, my nieces and nephews came over.

examples.tl: Huwag kang magkalat sa sala, may bisita tayo.
examples.en: Don't make a mess in the living room, we have guests.

notes: Nag-grocery, naggo-grocery, maggo-grocery. 'Grocery' also means the supermarket itself.

examples.tl: Mag-grocery tayo mamaya, wala nang laman ang ref.
examples.en: Let's do groceries later, the fridge is empty.

examples.tl: Nag-grocery ako sa SM, 3,000 ang nagastos ko.
examples.en: I did groceries at SM, I spent 3,000.

notes: Root palengke (wet market). Namalengke, namamalengke, mamamalengke.

examples.tl: Namalengke si Ate ng gulay at isda sa Guadalupe.
examples.en: Ate went to the market in Guadalupe for vegetables and fish.

examples.tl: Mas mura kung mamalengke ka kesa sa grocery.
examples.en: It's cheaper to shop at the market than the grocery.

notes: Root idlip. In Taglish people say 'mag-nap' or 'power nap'; 'siesta' also understood.

examples.tl: Umidlip lang ako pagkatapos ng lunch, tapos balik sa trabaho.
examples.en: I just napped after lunch, then back to work.

examples.tl: Iidlip muna ako, gisingin mo ako ng alas-tres.
examples.en: I'll nap for a bit, wake me at three.

notes: 'Buong araw' also means all day. 'Magdamag' = all night.

examples.tl: Maghapon akong nasa bahay, nag-WFH.
examples.en: I was home all day, working from home.

examples.tl: Maghapon na nakabukas ang aircon, patayin mo na.
examples.en: The aircon has been on all day, turn it off now.

notes: Reduplication pattern: gabi-gabi (every night), linggo-linggo (every week), umaga-umaga.

examples.tl: Araw-araw akong nag-jogging sa Ayala Triangle.
examples.en: I jog at Ayala Triangle every day.

examples.tl: Araw-araw ganito ang traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: The traffic on EDSA is like this every day.

notes: Tuwing umaga = every morning; tuwing Sabado = every Saturday. Also 'kada'.

examples.tl: Tuwing umaga, kape muna bago lahat.
examples.en: Every morning, coffee first before anything.

examples.tl: Tuwing Linggo kami naglilinis ng unit.
examples.en: We clean the unit every Sunday.

taglish: WFH ako bukas, kaya nasa condo lang ako.
notes: 'Nag-WFH ako' = I worked from home. Said as letters. Also just 'WFH ako bukas'.

examples.tl: Mag-WFH ako bukas, may inspection sa unit.
examples.en: I'll work from home tomorrow, there's an inspection in the unit.

examples.tl: Nag-WFH ako buong linggo, hindi ako lumabas.
examples.en: I worked from home all week, I didn't go out.

notes: Root pasok. Literally 'enter'; the usual word for going to work or class. 'Pasok' = work/class day.

examples.tl: Pumasok ka ba kahapon o nag-leave ka?
examples.en: Did you go to work yesterday or did you take leave?

examples.tl: May pasok ba bukas? Holiday daw.
examples.en: Is there work tomorrow? They say it's a holiday.

notes: Object focus of bukas. For doors, windows, lights, aircon, apps. 'Binuksan', 'binubuksan', 'bubuksan'.

examples.tl: Buksan mo ang aircon, ang init.
examples.en: Turn on the aircon, it's hot.

examples.tl: Pakibuksan ang pinto, wala akong susi.
examples.en: Please open the door, I don't have a key.

notes: Object focus of sara. For doors, windows, shops. Lights and appliances are 'patayin', not 'isara'.

examples.tl: Isara mo ang bintana, uulan.
examples.en: Close the window, it's going to rain.

examples.tl: Isinara na ng guard ang gate, late na tayo.
examples.en: The guard already closed the gate, we're late.

notes: Literally 'kill'. The normal word for switching off lights, aircon, phone, stove. Also 'i-off'.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang aircon kapag aalis ka.
examples.en: Turn off the aircon when you leave.

examples.tl: Pinatay ko ang cellphone ko sa sinehan.
examples.en: I turned off my phone in the cinema.

taglish: Na-lock ko ba ang pinto? Hindi ko maalala.
notes: 'I-lock mo' = lock it; 'naka-lock' = locked; 'na-lock out' = locked out. Native 'ikandado' is rarer in Manila.

examples.tl: I-lock mo ang pinto bago matulog.
examples.en: Lock the door before sleeping.

examples.tl: Naka-lock ang unit, nasa guard ang spare key.
examples.en: The unit is locked, the spare key is with the guard.

notes: Prepaid credit for Globe/Smart. 'Wala akong load' = I have no credit. Bought via GCash or sari-sari store.

examples.tl: Wala akong load, hindi ako maka-text.
examples.en: I have no credit, I can't text.

examples.tl: Pabili ng load, 100 Globe.
examples.en: Please buy me credit, 100 pesos Globe.

taglish: Mag-load muna ako sa GCash, wala na akong data.
notes: Nag-load, naglo-load, maglo-load. 'Pa-load' = please top me up.

examples.tl: Mag-load muna ako, wala na akong data.
examples.en: Let me top up first, I'm out of data.

examples.tl: Nag-load ako ng 99 para sa isang linggong promo.
examples.en: I topped up 99 pesos for the one-week promo.

notes: Root palit. 'Palitan mo' = replace/change it. 'Magpalit ng damit' = change clothes.

examples.tl: Magpalit ka ng damit, pawis ka.
examples.en: Change your clothes, you're sweaty.

examples.tl: Palitan mo na ang bedsheet, isang buwan na.
examples.en: Change the bedsheet already, it's been a month.

examples.tl: Magdamag akong hindi nakatulog, maingay ang kapitbahay.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep all night, the neighbors were noisy.

examples.tl: Magdamag na nakabukas ang ilaw sa sala.
examples.en: The living room light was on all night.

examples.tl: Masakit ang ulo ko, baka kulang sa tulog.
examples.en: My head hurts, maybe I lack sleep.

examples.tl: Naumpog ang ulo ko sa cabinet.
examples.en: I bumped my head on the cabinet.

examples.tl: Namumula ang mata mo, puyat ka ba?
examples.en: Your eyes are red, did you stay up late?

examples.tl: Masakit ang mata ko sa screen, maghapon sa laptop.
examples.en: My eyes hurt from the screen, all day on the laptop.

examples.tl: Barado ang ilong ko, may sipon ako.
examples.en: My nose is blocked, I have a cold.

examples.tl: Dumudugo ang ilong niya dahil sa init.
examples.en: His nose is bleeding because of the heat.

examples.tl: May singaw ako sa bibig, hindi ako makakain ng maanghang.
examples.en: I have a mouth sore, I can't eat spicy food.

examples.tl: Takpan mo ang bibig mo kapag umuubo.
examples.en: Cover your mouth when you cough.

examples.tl: Masakit ang ngipin ko, kailangan ko ng dentista.
examples.en: My tooth hurts, I need a dentist.

examples.tl: Magtoothbrush ka, may bawang sa ngipin mo.
examples.en: Brush your teeth, there's garlic in your teeth.

examples.tl: Masakit ang tiyan ko, baka sa kinain ko sa karinderya.
examples.en: My stomach hurts, maybe from what I ate at the eatery.

examples.tl: Kumukulo ang tiyan ko, gutom na ako.
examples.en: My stomach is growling, I'm hungry.

examples.tl: Maghugas ka ng kamay, galing ka sa jeep.
examples.en: Wash your hands, you came from the jeep.

examples.tl: Nasugatan ang kamay ko sa kutsilyo.
examples.en: I cut my hand on the knife.

notes: Covers foot and often the whole leg; 'binti' = lower leg, 'hita' = thigh.

examples.tl: Masakit ang paa ko, maghapon akong nakatayo.
examples.en: My feet hurt, I was standing all day.

examples.tl: Alisin mo ang sapatos, basa ang paa mo.
examples.en: Take off your shoes, your feet are wet.

notes: Also 'behind': 'sa likod ng building' = behind the building.

examples.tl: Masakit ang likod ko sa upuan sa office.
examples.en: My back hurts from the office chair.

examples.tl: Pakihilot ang likod ko, ang sakit.
examples.en: Please massage my back, it hurts.

examples.tl: Masakit ang balikat ko sa bag, sobrang bigat.
examples.en: My shoulder hurts from the bag, it's so heavy.

examples.tl: Stiff ang balikat ko, kailangan ko ng massage.
examples.en: My shoulders are stiff, I need a massage.

notes: Head hair only; body hair is 'balahibo'.

examples.tl: Basa pa ang buhok ko, hintayin mo ako.
examples.en: My hair is still wet, wait for me.

examples.tl: Magpapagupit ako ng buhok sa barbero sa may Guadalupe.
examples.en: I'll get a haircut at the barber near Guadalupe.

examples.tl: May sakit sa puso ang tatay ko, kaya bawal ang maalat.
examples.en: My father has heart disease, so no salty food.

examples.tl: Mabilis ang tibok ng puso ko pagkatapos ng hagdan.
examples.en: My heart was beating fast after the stairs.

examples.tl: Masakit ang leeg ko, maling unan.
examples.en: My neck hurts, wrong pillow.

examples.tl: Namamaga ang leeg niya, may lagnat din.
examples.en: His neck is swollen, he has a fever too.

examples.tl: Masakit ang tuhod ko pag-akyat ng hagdan.
examples.en: My knee hurts going up the stairs.

examples.tl: Nagasgas ang tuhod ko nung nadapa ako sa Ayala.
examples.en: I scraped my knee when I tripped at Ayala.

examples.tl: Masakit ang braso ko sa gym kahapon.
examples.en: My arms hurt from the gym yesterday.

examples.tl: Sunog ang braso ko, nakalimutan ang sunblock.
examples.en: My arm is sunburned, I forgot the sunblock.

notes: Also toes: 'daliri sa paa'.

examples.tl: Naipit ang daliri ko sa pinto.
examples.en: My finger got caught in the door.

examples.tl: Nahiwa ang daliri ko habang naghihiwa ng sibuyas.
examples.en: I cut my finger while slicing onions.

notes: Also 'mukhang' = looks like: 'mukhang pagod ka' = you look tired.

examples.tl: Maghilamos ka ng mukha, mamantika.
examples.en: Wash your face, it's oily.

examples.tl: Namumula ang mukha mo, ang init ba?
examples.en: Your face is red, is it the heat?

notes: Formal spelling 'tainga'; everyone says 'tenga'.

examples.tl: Masakit ang tenga ko pagkatapos ng flight.
examples.en: My ear hurts after the flight.

examples.tl: Nabingi ako sa karaoke ng kapitbahay, ang lakas sa tenga.
examples.en: The neighbor's karaoke deafened me, so loud in the ears.

examples.tl: Masakit ang lalamunan ko, baka sipon na ito.
examples.en: My throat hurts, this might be a cold coming.

examples.tl: May nakabara sa lalamunan ko, tinik ng bangus.
examples.en: Something's stuck in my throat, a milkfish bone.

notes: 'Masakit ang X ko' = my X hurts. Also emotional: 'masakit' = it hurts.

examples.tl: Masakit ang ulo ko, may Biogesic ka?
examples.en: My head hurts, do you have Biogesic?

examples.tl: Masakit ba? Punta tayo sa clinic.
examples.en: Does it hurt? Let's go to the clinic.

notes: 'Sakit ng ulo' = headache; 'may sakit' = sick. 'Ang sakit!' = ouch, it hurts!

examples.tl: Ang sakit! Naipit ang kamay ko.
examples.en: Ouch! My hand got caught.

examples.tl: Anong sakit niya? Dengue daw.
examples.en: What's his illness? They say dengue.

notes: 'May sakit ako' = I'm sick. 'Nagkasakit' = got sick. Also 'masama ang pakiramdam ko'.

examples.tl: May sakit si Ate, hindi siya makakapunta ngayon.
examples.en: Ate is sick, she can't come today.

examples.tl: May sakit ka ba? Mag-leave ka na lang.
examples.en: Are you sick? Just take the day off.

notes: Also figurative: a hassle ('sakit sa ulo' = pain in the neck).

examples.tl: May sakit ng ulo ako, uminom na ako ng gamot.
examples.en: I have a headache, I already took medicine.

examples.tl: Sakit sa ulo ang traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: The traffic on EDSA is a headache.

notes: 'May lagnat ako' or 'nilalagnat ako' = I have a fever.

examples.tl: May lagnat ako, 38.5 kanina.
examples.en: I have a fever, 38.5 earlier.

examples.tl: Mataas pa ang lagnat niya, dalhin natin sa ospital.
examples.en: His fever is still high, let's take him to the hospital.

notes: Verb form of lagnat. Nilagnat (had a fever), nilalagnat (has), lalagnatin (will).

examples.tl: Nilalagnat ako kaya hindi ako papasok.
examples.en: I have a fever so I won't go to work.

examples.tl: Nilagnat ako ng tatlong araw pagkatapos ng bakuna.
examples.en: I had a fever for three days after the vaccine.

notes: 'Umubo' = to cough; 'inuubo ako' = I have a cough.

examples.tl: Inuubo ako, dalawang linggo na.
examples.en: I've had a cough for two weeks now.

examples.tl: May ubo at sipon ang anak ko, baka trangkaso.
examples.en: My child has a cough and cold, maybe flu.

notes: 'May sipon ako' or 'sinisipon ako' = I have a cold. Not 'malamig'.

examples.tl: May sipon ako, dahil sa aircon sa office.
examples.en: I have a cold, because of the office aircon.

examples.tl: Sinisipon ako, pahingi ng tissue.
examples.en: I have a runny nose, can I have a tissue.

notes: 'Pagod na ako' = I'm tired. 'Napagod' = got tired. 'Nakakapagod' = tiring.

examples.tl: Pagod na ako, uwi na tayo.
examples.en: I'm tired, let's go home.

examples.tl: Nakakapagod ang commute mula Makati hanggang QC.
examples.en: The commute from Makati to QC is exhausting.

notes: 'Inaantok ako' = I'm sleepy (the usual form). 'Antok na ako' also fine.

examples.tl: Inaantok ako sa meeting, kape muna.
examples.en: I'm sleepy in the meeting, coffee first.

examples.tl: Antok na ako, tulog na ako. Good night!
examples.en: I'm sleepy, going to sleep. Good night!

notes: 'Gutom na ako' or 'nagugutom ako' = I'm hungry.

examples.tl: Gutom na ako, order na tayo sa Grab.
examples.en: I'm hungry, let's order on Grab.

examples.tl: Nagugutom ako kapag amoy sinigang.
examples.en: I get hungry when I smell sinigang.

notes: 'Uhaw ako' or 'nauuhaw ako'.

examples.tl: Uhaw ako, may tubig ka?
examples.en: I'm thirsty, do you have water?

examples.tl: Nauuhaw ako sa init, bili tayo ng buko juice.
examples.en: I'm thirsty from the heat, let's buy coconut juice.

notes: 'Busog na ako' = I'm full. 'Nakakabusog' = filling.

examples.tl: Busog na ako, ikaw na ang tumapos.
examples.en: I'm full, you finish it.

examples.tl: Nakakabusog ang unli rice sa Mang Inasal.
examples.en: The unlimited rice at Mang Inasal is filling.

notes: 'Nahihilo ako' = I'm dizzy. Also for motion sickness.

examples.tl: Nahihilo ako sa bus, bukas mo ang bintana.
examples.en: I'm getting dizzy on the bus, open the window.

examples.tl: Nahihilo ako sa init, kailangan ko ng tubig.
examples.en: I'm dizzy from the heat, I need water.

notes: Root suka (vomit). 'Sumuka' = to vomit, 'nagsuka' also.

examples.tl: Nasusuka ako, sobrang amoy ng usok ng jeep.
examples.en: I feel nauseous, the jeep fumes smell so strong.

examples.tl: Sumuka siya pagkatapos uminom kagabi.
examples.en: He threw up after drinking last night.

notes: 'Uminom ng gamot' = take medicine (literally drink). Biogesic = paracetamol brand everyone names.

examples.tl: Uminom ka na ng gamot bago matulog.
examples.en: Take your medicine before you sleep.

examples.tl: May gamot ka ba sa sakit ng ulo?
examples.en: Do you have medicine for a headache?

notes: Address as 'Doc'. 'Magpa-doktor' = see a doctor. 'Doktora' for a woman.

examples.tl: Magpa-doktor ka na, isang linggo ka nang inuubo.
examples.en: Go see a doctor, you've been coughing for a week.

examples.tl: Ano ang sabi ng doktor? Rest lang daw.
examples.en: What did the doctor say? Just rest, he said.

notes: Makati Med, St. Luke's BGC, etc. 'Na-ospital' = got hospitalized.

examples.tl: Dinala siya sa ospital kagabi, dehydrated.
examples.en: He was taken to the hospital last night, dehydrated.

examples.tl: Malapit ang Makati Med sa condo, pwedeng lakarin.
examples.en: Makati Med is close to the condo, you can walk.

notes: Many just say 'Mercury' (Mercury Drug) or 'drugstore'. 'Parmasya' is formal.

examples.tl: Bibili lang ako ng paracetamol sa botika.
examples.en: I'll just buy paracetamol at the pharmacy.

examples.tl: May 24-hour na Mercury sa Guadalupe.
examples.en: There's a 24-hour Mercury Drug in Guadalupe.

taglish: Magpapa-check-up ako bukas, covered ng HMO.
notes: 'Magpa-check-up' = get a check-up. HMO = health insurance card.

examples.tl: May check-up ako sa doktor bukas ng umaga.
examples.en: I have a check-up with the doctor tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Magpa-check-up ka na, matagal na yang ubo mo.
examples.en: Get a check-up, that cough has been going on a while.

notes: Sumakit (hurt), sumasakit (hurts/is hurting), sasakit (will hurt).

examples.tl: Sumakit ang tiyan ko pagkatapos kumain ng street food.
examples.en: My stomach started hurting after eating street food.

examples.tl: Sumasakit ang ulo ko kapag kulang ako sa tubig.
examples.en: My head aches when I don't drink enough water.

notes: 'Gumaling' = got well. 'Magaling' alone = skilled/good at something.

examples.tl: Magaling na ako, pwede na akong pumasok.
examples.en: I'm better now, I can go to work.

examples.tl: Gumaling na ba ang anak mo? Lagnat daw.
examples.en: Has your child recovered? He had a fever, you said.

notes: 'Nasugatan' = got wounded. Betadine and Band-Aid are the usual words for fixing it.

examples.tl: May sugat ako sa paa, lagyan ko ng Betadine.
examples.en: I have a cut on my foot, I'll put Betadine on it.

examples.tl: Nasugatan ang kamay niya sa lata.
examples.en: His hand got cut on the can.

notes: 'May allergy ako sa X' = I'm allergic to X. 'Allergic ako sa hipon' also used.

examples.tl: May allergy ako sa hipon, huwag mo lagyan.
examples.en: I'm allergic to shrimp, don't add any.

examples.tl: Nag-allergy siya sa alikabok, puro bahing.
examples.en: He had an allergy to the dust, kept sneezing.

notes: 'Pawis na pawis ako' = I'm drenched in sweat. 'Pinagpapawisan' = sweating.

examples.tl: Pawis na pawis ako, ang init sa labas.
examples.en: I'm drenched in sweat, it's so hot outside.

examples.tl: Magpalit ka, basa ng pawis ang damit mo.
examples.en: Change, your shirt is wet with sweat.

notes: Root ihi. Umihi, umiihi, iihi. 'Iihi lang ako' = I'll just pee. 'Mag-CR' is the polite way.

examples.tl: Iihi lang ako, saan ang CR?
examples.en: I'll just pee, where's the restroom?

examples.tl: Umihi muna ang bata bago umalis.
examples.en: The kid peed first before leaving.

notes: 'Kumusta ang pakiramdam mo?' = how are you feeling? 'Pakiramdam ko' = I feel like.

examples.tl: Kumusta ang pakiramdam mo? Okay na ba?
examples.en: How are you feeling? Okay now?

examples.tl: Pakiramdam ko lalagnatin ako.
examples.en: I feel like I'm coming down with a fever.

notes: The standard way to say you feel sick. Opposite: 'maganda ang pakiramdam ko'.

examples.tl: Masama ang pakiramdam ko, mag-leave ako ngayon.
examples.en: I don't feel well, I'll take leave today.

examples.tl: Masama ang pakiramdam ni Ate, hindi siya makakapaglinis.
examples.en: Ate feels unwell, she won't be able to clean.

notes: Root ginaw. Say this, not 'malamig ako'. 'Nilalamig' is also heard.

examples.tl: Giniginaw ako, hinaan mo ang aircon.
examples.en: I'm cold, turn down the aircon.

examples.tl: Giniginaw siya pero may lagnat, baka trangkaso.
examples.en: He feels cold but has a fever, might be flu.

notes: Root init. Say this, not 'mainit ako' (which sounds odd). 'Ang init!' = it's so hot!

examples.tl: Naiinitan ako, buksan natin ang aircon.
examples.en: I'm hot, let's turn on the aircon.

examples.tl: Naiinitan ang bata, patayin mo ang kalan.
examples.en: The kid is hot, turn off the stove.

notes: Very common word with no English equivalent. 'Napuyat ako' = I stayed up late / lacked sleep.

examples.tl: Puyat ako, alas-tres na natulog dahil sa deadline.
examples.en: I'm sleep-deprived, slept at three because of the deadline.

examples.tl: Mukhang puyat ka, kape ka muna.
examples.en: You look like you lack sleep, have coffee first.

notes: Any garment or clothes in general. 'Magdamit' = to dress.

examples.tl: Dami ng damit sa sala, ligpitin mo.
examples.en: So many clothes in the living room, put them away.

examples.tl: Bili ako ng bagong damit sa Uniqlo, sale.
examples.en: I bought new clothes at Uniqlo, there was a sale.

notes: 'Jeans' is also just 'jeans'. 'Maong' = denim.

examples.tl: Basa ang pantalon ko sa ulan, magpapalit ako.
examples.en: My pants got wet in the rain, I'll change.

examples.tl: Bawal ang shorts sa office, pantalon dapat.
examples.en: Shorts aren't allowed at the office, must be pants.

notes: Said in English. Standard condo and weekend wear in the heat.

examples.tl: Shorts at tsinelas lang ako, lalabas lang sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Just shorts and slippers for me, only going out to 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Bawal ang shorts sa simbahan.
examples.en: Shorts are not allowed in church.

notes: 'Rubber shoes' = sneakers. Take them off at the door in most homes.

examples.tl: Alisin mo ang sapatos sa pinto, bago ang sahig.
examples.en: Take off your shoes at the door, the floor is new.

examples.tl: Basa ang sapatos ko, baha sa Buendia.
examples.en: My shoes are wet, there was flooding on Buendia.

notes: Flip-flops; everyone has a pair by the door. 'Pang-bahay' = house slippers.

examples.tl: Magtsinelas ka sa loob, malamig ang sahig.
examples.en: Wear slippers inside, the floor is cold.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang tsinelas ko? Nasa may pinto?
examples.en: Where are my slippers? By the door?

examples.tl: Wala akong malinis na medyas, hindi pa nalabhan.
examples.en: I have no clean socks, they haven't been washed.

examples.tl: Nawawala ang isang medyas ko, baka sa washing machine.
examples.en: One of my socks is missing, maybe in the washing machine.

notes: For a baseball cap people say 'cap'. Sombrero = any hat, often a wide one.

examples.tl: Magsuot ka ng sombrero, sobrang init ng araw.
examples.en: Wear a hat, the sun is really hot.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang cap ko sa Grab.
examples.en: I left my cap in the Grab.

notes: Both wristwatch and wall clock. 'Anong oras na sa relo mo?'

examples.tl: Anong oras na sa relo mo? Patay ang cellphone ko.
examples.en: What time is it on your watch? My phone is dead.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang relo ko sa banyo.
examples.en: I forgot my watch in the bathroom.

notes: Both eyeglasses and mirror. 'Shades' = sunglasses.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang salamin ko? Hindi ko mabasa ang menu.
examples.en: Where are my glasses? I can't read the menu.

examples.tl: May salamin sa pinto ng aparador.
examples.en: There's a mirror on the wardrobe door.

notes: Said in English. 'Bantayan mo ang bag ko' = watch my bag.

examples.tl: Bantayan mo ang bag ko, mag-CR lang ako.
examples.en: Watch my bag, I'll just use the restroom.

examples.tl: Nasa bag ko ang susi at wallet.
examples.en: The key and wallet are in my bag.

notes: Said in English. 'Pitaka' is the native word, still used by older people.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa condo, pahiram muna ng pamasahe.
examples.en: I left my wallet at the condo, lend me fare money.

examples.tl: Wala akong cash sa wallet, GCash lang.
examples.en: I have no cash in my wallet, just GCash.

notes: Carry one always: for rain and for the sun. 'Magpayong' = use an umbrella.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang payong, uulan mamaya.
examples.en: Bring the umbrella, it'll rain later.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ulit ang payong ko sa jeep, ilang beses na ito.
examples.en: I left my umbrella in the jeep again, this has happened several times.

notes: 'Shirt' or 't-shirt' in English. 'Sando' = sleeveless undershirt.

examples.tl: T-shirt at shorts lang ako sa bahay.
examples.en: I just wear a t-shirt and shorts at home.

examples.tl: Puro puting t-shirt ang binili ko, mura sa Divisoria.
examples.en: I bought all white t-shirts, cheap in Divisoria.

notes: In the Philippines 'polo' = a collared button-down, not a polo shirt. 'Polo shirt' = the golf type.

examples.tl: Polo ang suot ko sa office, hindi t-shirt.
examples.en: I wear a collared shirt at the office, not a t-shirt.

examples.tl: Paki-plantsa ang polo ko, may meeting ako bukas.
examples.en: Please iron my shirt, I have a meeting tomorrow.

notes: Worn mostly for aircon in malls, cinemas and offices, not for weather.

examples.tl: Magdala ka ng jacket, malamig sa sinehan.
examples.en: Bring a jacket, it's cold in the cinema.

examples.tl: Bakit may jacket ka, 35 degrees sa labas?
examples.en: Why do you have a jacket on, it's 35 degrees outside?

notes: Root suot. Nagsuot, nagsusuot, magsusuot. 'Isuot mo' = wear it. 'Suot' = outfit.

examples.tl: Magsuot ka ng jacket, malamig sa office.
examples.en: Wear a jacket, it's cold at the office.

examples.tl: Anong isusuot ko sa party? Smart casual daw.
examples.en: What should I wear to the party? Smart casual, they said.

notes: For clothes, furniture, people in a car. 'Hindi kasya' = doesn't fit. 'Kumasya' = did fit.

examples.tl: Hindi na kasya ang jeans ko, dami ng kinain sa Pasko.
examples.en: My jeans don't fit anymore, I ate too much at Christmas.

examples.tl: Kasya ba ang sofa sa elevator?
examples.en: Will the sofa fit in the elevator?

notes: Filipinos say 'cellphone' or 'phone', texted as 'cp'. Never 'mobile'.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang cellphone ko? Nasa kama?
examples.en: Where's my phone? On the bed?

examples.tl: Nabasag ang screen ng cellphone ko, nalaglag sa jeep.
examples.en: My phone screen cracked, it fell in the jeep.

notes: Said in English. 'Pahiram ng charger' is a daily phrase.

examples.tl: Pahiram ng charger, lowbat na ako.
examples.en: Lend me a charger, my battery's low.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang charger ko sa office.
examples.en: I left my charger at the office.

notes: Nag-charge, nagcha-charge, magcha-charge. 'I-charge mo' = charge it. 'Naka-charge' = charging/plugged in.

examples.tl: Mag-charge muna ako, lowbat na ako.
examples.en: Let me charge first, my battery's low.

examples.tl: I-charge mo ang powerbank bago tayo umalis.
examples.en: Charge the powerbank before we leave.

notes: From 'low battery'. Also jokingly for a tired person: 'lowbat na ako'.

examples.tl: Lowbat na ako, mag-text ka lang kung saan tayo magkikita.
examples.en: My battery's low, just text me where we'll meet.

examples.tl: Lowbat ang cellphone ko kaya hindi ako nakasagot.
examples.en: My phone was low on battery so I couldn't answer.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang laptop, mag-WFH tayo sa coffee shop.
examples.en: Bring the laptop, let's work from a coffee shop.

examples.tl: Namatay ang laptop ko sa gitna ng meeting.
examples.en: My laptop died in the middle of the meeting.

notes: Pronounced 'tee-vee'. 'Manood ng TV' = watch TV.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang TV, walang nanonood.
examples.en: Turn off the TV, nobody's watching.

examples.tl: Nanood lang kami ng TV buong Linggo.
examples.en: We just watched TV all Sunday.

notes: For the TV and the aircon. 'Nasaan ang remote?' is heard in every Filipino home.

examples.tl: Nasaan ang remote ng aircon?
examples.en: Where's the aircon remote?

examples.tl: Ubos na ang baterya ng remote, bili ka ng AA.
examples.en: The remote's batteries are dead, buy some AA.

notes: 'Mabagal ang wifi' = the wifi is slow. PLDT, Globe, Converge are the providers.

examples.tl: Mabagal ang wifi, umuulan kasi.
examples.en: The wifi is slow, because it's raining.

examples.tl: Ano ang password ng wifi niyo?
examples.en: What's your wifi password?

notes: Pronounced 'day-ta'. 'Wala akong data' = I'm out of mobile data. Bought as 'promo' with load.

examples.tl: Wala akong data, hindi ako maka-Grab.
examples.en: I have no data, I can't book a Grab.

examples.tl: Mag-data ka lang, walang wifi sa jeep.
examples.en: Just use your data, there's no wifi on the jeep.

notes: Root saksak (also 'stab'). 'Nakasaksak' = plugged in. 'Tanggalin sa saksakan' = unplug.

examples.tl: Isaksak mo ang charger sa extension.
examples.en: Plug the charger into the power strip.

examples.tl: Nakasaksak pa ba ang plantsa? Tanggalin mo.
examples.en: Is the iron still plugged in? Unplug it.

notes: Also just 'outlet'. Philippines uses 220V with US-style flat plugs.

examples.tl: May saksakan ba malapit sa mesa? Kailangan ko mag-charge.
examples.en: Is there an outlet near the table? I need to charge.

examples.tl: Kulang ang saksakan sa kwarto, bili ka ng extension.
examples.en: Not enough outlets in the room, buy a power strip.

notes: 'Extension' or 'extension cord' = power strip. Every condo desk has one.

examples.tl: Pahiram ng extension, isa lang ang saksakan dito.
examples.en: Lend me a power strip, there's only one outlet here.

examples.tl: Huwag mong isaksak ang aircon sa extension, delikado.
examples.en: Don't plug the aircon into the extension, it's dangerous.

examples.tl: Ano ang password ng wifi? Nasa router?
examples.en: What's the wifi password? On the router?

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang password ng GCash ko.
examples.en: I forgot my GCash password.

notes: Essential for brownouts and long commutes.

examples.tl: Dala ka ng powerbank, mahaba ang biyahe.
examples.en: Bring a power bank, it's a long trip.

examples.tl: Naka-charge na ang powerbank, nasa mesa.
examples.en: The power bank is charged, it's on the table.

notes: Standing wardrobe or cabinet. Many just say 'cabinet' or 'closet'.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa aparador ang mga naplantsang damit.
examples.en: Put the ironed clothes in the wardrobe.

examples.tl: Puno na ang aparador, mag-donate ka ng damit.
examples.en: The wardrobe is full, donate some clothes.

notes: The condo unit phone to the lobby or guard.

examples.tl: Tumawag ang guard sa intercom, may bisita ka.
examples.en: The guard called on the intercom, you have a visitor.

examples.tl: Sira ang intercom namin, text na lang sa guard.
examples.en: Our intercom is broken, we just text the guard.

notes: Root kalat. Nagkalat, nagkakalat, magkakalat. 'Nagkalat' also = is lying around everywhere.

examples.tl: Huwag kang magkalat sa kusina, kakalinis lang ni Ate.
examples.en: Don't make a mess in the kitchen, Ate just cleaned.

examples.tl: Nagkalat ang mga damit sa sahig.
examples.en: Clothes are scattered on the floor.

notes: 'Mag-leave' = take a day off; 'SL' = sick leave, 'VL' = vacation leave.

examples.tl: Mag-sick leave ka na lang, may lagnat ka.
examples.en: Just take sick leave, you have a fever.

examples.tl: Nag-SL ako kahapon, masama ang pakiramdam ko.
examples.en: I took sick leave yesterday, I felt unwell.

notes: Traditional Filipino massage; also the masseuse. 'Magpahilot' = get a massage. Spas say 'massage'.

examples.tl: Magpapahilot ako, masakit ang likod ko.
examples.en: I'll get a massage, my back hurts.

examples.tl: May hilot sa may palengke, 300 lang.
examples.en: There's a masseuse near the market, only 300.

notes: 'Magpa-dentista' = go to the dentist. Also 'dentist'.

examples.tl: Magpa-dentista ka na, matagal nang masakit ang ngipin mo.
examples.en: Go to the dentist, your tooth has hurt for a long time.

examples.tl: May appointment ako sa dentista sa Sabado, cleaning lang.
examples.en: I have a dentist appointment on Saturday, just a cleaning.

notes: Said in English. 'Uminom ng vitamins' = take vitamins.

examples.tl: Uminom ka ng vitamins araw-araw para hindi magkasakit.
examples.en: Take vitamins every day so you don't get sick.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan ko ang vitamins ko ngayong umaga.
examples.en: I forgot my vitamins this morning.

notes: Root hilamos. Specific to the face; hands = maghugas, body = maligo.

examples.tl: Maghilamos ka muna, may muta ka pa.
examples.en: Wash your face first, you still have eye gunk.

examples.tl: Naghilamos lang ako, hindi na ako naligo.
examples.en: I just washed my face, I didn't shower anymore.

notes: Native word; 'sipilyo' = toothbrush. In Manila 'mag-toothbrush' is more common.

examples.tl: Magsipilyo ka bago matulog.
examples.en: Brush your teeth before sleeping.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng bagong sipilyo, luma na yan.
examples.en: Buy a new toothbrush, that one's old.

taglish: Nag-mop na ako ng sahig, huwag kang tumapak muna.
notes: Nag-mop, nagmo-mop, magmo-mop. The mop itself is 'mop'.

examples.tl: Mag-mop ka ng sahig pagkatapos magwalis.
examples.en: Mop the floor after sweeping.

examples.tl: Basa pa ang sahig, kaka-mop lang.
examples.en: The floor is still wet, it was just mopped.

notes: Said in English. 'Sapin' = sheet/lining; 'kobre-kama' is old-fashioned.

examples.tl: Palitan mo ang bedsheet, Linggo na.
examples.en: Change the bedsheet, it's Sunday.

examples.tl: Nasa labahan ang bedsheet, gamitin mo muna ang luma.
examples.en: The bedsheet is in the wash, use the old one for now.

notes: Said in English. 'Balkonahe' is the Tagalog word, rarely used in Manila.

examples.tl: Bawal magsampay sa balcony, sabi ng admin.
examples.en: No hanging laundry on the balcony, says the admin.

examples.tl: Nag-kape ako sa balcony, ganda ng view ng BGC.
examples.en: I had coffee on the balcony, great view of BGC.
